items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: The interviewee (Bob Watts) does not speak in the provided context. The interviewer mentions 'Bruce' and asks 'Did he? Oh, yeah. Melvin's more sandals, but he used to be on a ship with Melvin.' The interviewee's response 'Oh, yeah' confirms knowledge of Bruce's connection to Melvin Wright, but there

ctx.x: But we ain't know but six numbers. That's all we knew. That's all they knew, you know? And we go over and over, and you couldn't get in Mr. Clayton's place. Couldn't get in there. And them boys would be coming down there, sitting down there looking at us playing about 10 o'clock. And them boys had a wonderful band. We'd go down there to their rehearsal. None of our band could read, you know? We were just listening. Wonderful band. But you tried to- But he said they got there. The man said, well, I said, I wish I…

Leo, I mean, Melvin Wright died, huh? That's what they say. Yeah, that's what Bruce told me. You know Bruce, the tenor player from San Francisco? Who? Bruce, the tenor player from San Francisco. He used to hang around preservation halls. Did he? Oh, yeah. Melvin's more sandals, but he used to be on a ship with Melvin.
Yeah, he'd run out of Frisco. Yeah. Yeah. He'd run out of Frisco. Yeah, Melvin Wright. I think he was deceased.
